chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad narrated from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from a man, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
Whoever wishes to be granted offspring, let him pray two rak'ahs after Friday prayer, lengthening the bowing and prostration in them.
Then he should say: 'O Allah, I ask You by what Zakariya asked You, when he said, "My Lord, do not leave me solitary, and You are the best of inheritors."'
O Allah, grant me good offspring. Indeed, You are the Hearer of supplication.
O Allah, by Your name I made it lawful for myself, and by Your trust I took it. If You have decreed a child in her womb, then make it a boy, and do not give Satan any share or partnership in him.
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended prayer and supplication for having children in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith prescribes a specific two-rak'ah prayer after Friday prayers, emphasizing prolonged bowing and prostration to seek offspring. It uniquely integrates the supplication of Prophet Zakariya with a practical invocation for the child's gender and protection from Satan, reflecting the Shia tradition of combining Quranic precedent with specific ritual acts (fiqh al-du'a).
